newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says PLO policeman shot at patrol in Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Israel says PLO policeman shot at patrol in Gaza.

text.p: Israel said it had apprehended a Palestinian policeman who shot at Israeli troops patrolling near a Jewish settlement in the Gaza Strip on Thursday.
But a Palestinian official denied the policeman had fired his gun and said he was pursuing a suspected Palestinian smuggler when Israelis detained him.
No one was injured in the incident.
"A Palestinan policeman was arrested this evening by soldiers after he fired at soldiers on routine patrol on the road separating Khan Younis and Gush Katif (settlement) in Gaza," the spokesman said.
Israel filed a complaint with Palestinian officials at a joint coordinating office in Gaza, he said.
Palestinian Major General Abdel Razek al-Majayda said the four policemen were chasing a suspected smuggler who fired several shots in the air while being pursued.
He said Israeli troops arrested one of the policemen and the supect fled.
"We demand a joint investigation and the immediate release of the detained Palestinian policeman who never fired his gun," Majayda told Reuters.
Israel handed over most of the Gaza Strip to Palestinian rule in 1994 under a peace deal with the PLO. Israeli soldiers still patrol around Jewish settlements and on main roads.
